# Memory

::: {.callout-question}
How does an embodied agent maintain spatial belief under sensor occlusion and predict future states without the computational overhead of high-fidelity 3D physics rendering?
:::

![Systems Organ Focus: Stage 3 (World Models, Latent Predictive Dynamics & Spatial $SE(3)$ State).](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.pdf){#fig-locator-ch05 width=100%}

::: {.callout-objective}
By the conclusion of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Construct Continuous Temporal Belief Buffers:** Bridge discrete, staggered sensor arrivals with high-frequency forward prediction loops.
2. **Deploy Latent World Models:** Implement non-generative predictive architectures (JEPA, RSSM) that anticipate future dynamics directly in representation space.
3. **Maintain Dynamic $SE(3)$ Frame Trees:** Perform continuous spatial coordinate transformations and smooth Lie algebra ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$) tangent-space integration.
4. **Enforce State Validity TTL Leases:** Quantify state uncertainty decay and revoke physical authority when sensory evidence expires.
5. **Freeze the State and Timing Model (`STATE-01`):** Construct the fifth artifact of the Cumulative Design Dossier establishing spatial coordinate graphs and validity bounds.
:::

::: {.callout-autopsy}
* **System:** Precision Electronic Assembly Arm (3-DoF Delta Robot)
* **Incident:** Gripper slammed into aluminum PCB jig; shattered suction nozzle.
* **Telemetry Snapshot:** Camera detected target PCB position at $T+08.100\text{ s}$. Due to USB transfer buffering, the vision transform matrix was stamped $65\text{ ms}$ in the past.
* **Root Cause:** The arm forward-kinematics tree was evaluated using current joint angles but historical camera frames without synchronizing coordinate frame timestamps.
* **Architectural Flaw:** The system lacked an $SE(3)$ time-indexed temporal belief buffer.
:::

::: {.callout-contract}
| Component | Authority and Substrate | Contract Specification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **What the MPU Proposes (System 2)** | *Untrusted · Stochastic · Linux MPU* | • Estimated world state: $s_t = [x, v, q, \dot{q}, \Sigma]$<br>• Spatial frame transform: $T_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)$<br>• Uncertainty covariance bounds: $\text{Tr}(\Sigma) \le \sigma_{\text{max}}$ |
| **What the MCU Permits (System 1)** | *Trusted · Deterministic · Real-Time MCU* | • Verifies state lease is fresh: $(t_{\text{now}} - t_{\text{upd}}) < \tau_{\text{TTL}}$<br>• Checks innovation residuals: $\|z - h(x)\| < 3\sigma$<br>• Enforces dynamic thermal derating: $\tau \le \tau_{\text{max}}(T)$ |
| **Failure Escalation** | *MCU Hardware Reflex* | If spatial uncertainty exceeds threshold, freeze state lease and command Category 2 safe position hold. |
:::

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
**The Sim-to-Real Delta:**
* **What Simulation Assumes:** Robot base and world origin share a static, perfect transformation matrix; joint state is known with mathematical certainty at every simulation step.
* **What the Bench Measures:** Camera mounting brackets flex under mechanical acceleration; microsecond clock drift between sensor microcontrollers causes artificial velocity estimation spikes; state uncertainty grows exponentially during visual occlusion.
:::

---

## Discrete Observations vs. Continuous Temporal Belief

The physical world evolves continuously: $\dot{x} = f(x, u)$. Sensors sample this continuum at discrete, staggered intervals.

| Sensory Stream / State Model | Arrival Rate & Jitter | Temporal Synchronization & Propagation Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **High-Rate Proprioception**<br>*(IMU: 1 kHz, Encoders: 200 Hz)* | Hard real-time ($< 0.1\text{ ms}$ jitter) | Direct MCU timer capture; provides the continuous high-frequency base for numerical forward-integration. |
| **Delayed Exteroception**<br>*(Stereo Depth / Vision: 30 Hz)* | Delayed arrival ($30\text{--}80\text{ ms}$ lag) | Ingested with PTP hardware timestamps; historical state ring buffer rewinds to $t_{\text{capture}}$, applies Kalman innovation updates, and re-propagates forward to $t_{\text{now}}$. |
| **Continuous Temporal Belief $S(t)$** | Continuous ($1000\text{ Hz}$ query rate) | Forward prediction buffer continuously solves $\dot{x} = f(x, u)$ between discrete sensor arrivals to eliminate control staleness. |

To bridge the gap between sensor arrivals:

1. **The Prediction Buffer:** The system integrates kinematic equations of motion to forward-predict the machine's current state $S(t_{\text{now}})$ in real time.
2. **Measurement Updates:** When delayed observations arrive ($O_{t-\text{lag}}$), the state history buffer rewinds, applies innovation corrections, and forward-propagates the updated belief to the present instant.

---

## Spatial Coordinate Frame Trees ($SE(3)$) and Lie Algebra ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$)

Every physical measurement is referenced to a specific physical coordinate frame. The machine maintains a dynamic **Spatial Frame Graph**:

| Coordinate Frame Pair | Physical Meaning & Transform Notation | Calibration & Update Frequency |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **World $\to$ Robot Base** | $T_{\text{base}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)$ (Odometry localization) | Continuous EKF integration ($200\text{ Hz}$) |
| **Base $\to$ Camera** | $T_{\text{camera}}^{\text{base}} \in SE(3)$ (Extrinsic sensor mounting) | Rigid kinematic calibration (Static / thermal drift tracking) |
| **Base $\to$ End-Effector** | $T_{\text{EE}}^{\text{base}} \in SE(3)$ (Forward kinematics) | Real-time joint encoder computation ($1000\text{ Hz}$) |
| **Camera $\to$ Target Object** | $T_{\text{target}}^{\text{camera}} \in SE(3)$ (Visual affordance detection) | Stochastic VLM/Perception proposal updates ($10\text{--}30\text{ Hz}$) |
| **End-Effector $\to$ Grasp** | $T_{\text{grasp}}^{\text{EE}} \in SE(3)$ (Tactile contact offset) | Tactile contact detection and force closure ($1000\text{ Hz}$) |

A rigid body transformation between frame $A$ and frame $B$ is represented as a homogeneous matrix in the Special Euclidean group $T_B^A \in SE(3)$:

$$T_B^A = \begin{bmatrix} R_B^A & p_B^A \\ 0_{1\times 3} & 1 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{4 \times 4}$$

### Tangent Space Integration ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$)
To integrate continuous velocities without encountering Euler angle gimbal lock singularities, updates are computed in the Lie algebra tangent space ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$):

$$T(t + \Delta t) = T(t) \cdot \exp(\xi^\wedge \cdot \Delta t)$$

Where $\xi = [v, \omega]^T \in \mathbb{R}^6$ represents the combined linear and angular twist vector.

---

## The Predict-Observe-Correct Estimator Cycle

From a systems engineering perspective, state estimation is a 3-step continuous cycle:

| Estimator Step | Mathematical Computation | Physical & Systems Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Predict** *(Forward Model)* | $\hat{x}_t = f(\hat{x}_{t-1}, u_{t-1})$, $P_t = F P_{t-1} F^T + Q$ | Propagates belief continuously across inter-sensor arrival intervals ($1000\text{ Hz}$). |
| **2. Observe** *(Innovation Residual)* | $y_t = z_t - h(\hat{x}_t)$, $S_t = H P_t H^T + R$ | Evaluates statistical discrepancy between sensory evidence and forward belief. Serves as a hardware anomaly flag. |
| **3. Correct** *(Covariance Update)* | $K_t = P_t H^T S_t^{-1}$, $\hat{x}_t \leftarrow \hat{x}_t + K_t y_t$ | Fuses delayed measurement and tightens spatial uncertainty covariance $P_t$. |

* **Innovation Residuals ($y = z - h(\hat{x})$):** If the residual suddenly exceeds statistical bounds ($\|y\| > 3\sigma$), the system detects sensor occlusion, encoder slip, or external mechanical collision.

---

## Proprioceptive State and Interoceptive Health (Thermal Derating)

In addition to external spatial coordinates, the state model tracks internal physical health:

1. **Proprioception:** Joint angles ($q$), joint velocities ($\dot{q}$), actuator torques ($\tau$), and contact forces ($F_{\text{contact}}$).
2. **Interoception:** Motor winding temperatures ($T_{\text{motor}}$), battery voltage sag ($V_{\text{bus}}$), and inverter current draw.

| Operating Thermal Regime | Winding Temperature Range | Maximum Permissible Torque $\tau_{\text{max}}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nominal Operating Zone** | $T_{\text{motor}} < 85^\circ\text{C}$ | $100\%$ nominal continuous torque rated authority. |
| **Linear Derating Zone** | $85^\circ\text{C} \le T_{\text{motor}} \le 110^\circ\text{C}$ | Linearly derated: $\tau_{\text{max}}(T) = \tau_{\text{nom}} \cdot \left(1 - \frac{T - 85}{25}\right)$. |
| **Thermal Emergency Cutoff** | $T_{\text{motor}} > 110^\circ\text{C}$ | $\tau = 0\text{ Nm}$; open inverter gate drives to prevent permanent winding demagnetization. |

When winding temperature climbs toward thermal limits ($T > 85^\circ\text{C}$), the state model dynamically derates the maximum allowable actuator torque ($\tau_{\text{max}}(T)$) to prevent permanent motor demagnetization.

---

## State Validity Horizons (TTL Leases) and Drift Triggers

Internal belief degrades over time if not refreshed by new physical evidence. Every state estimate carries a strict **Time-To-Live (TTL) lease**:

$$\text{State Lease Valid If: } (t_{\text{now}} - t_{\text{last\_sensor\_update}}) < \tau_{\text{TTL}}$$

If no valid sensory evidence arrives before $\tau_{\text{TTL}}$ expires, the state model triggers a **State Drift Alarm**, invalidating downstream neural proposals and commanding safe fallback.

---

## Systems Fallacies and Pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning}
### Common Engineering Fallacies
* **Fallacy 1:** *"The internal latent representation of an LLM or VLM acts as a spatial world model."*  
  *Correction:* Neural context windows do not maintain metric spatial coordinates, frame graphs, or physical velocity integration.
* **Fallacy 2:** *"Euler angles are suitable for robot orientation representation."*  
  *Correction:* Euler angles suffer from mathematical singularities (gimbal lock); orientation must be parameterized using unit quaternions or Lie group matrices ($SO(3)$).
:::

---

::: {.callout-decision}
### Dossier Delta: State, Frames and Timing Model (`STATE-01`)
Freeze the internal state representations:

1. The $SE(3)$ coordinate frame tree hierarchy and baseline calibration transforms.
2. State vector schemas (pose, velocity, covariance, proprioceptive currents, and thermal health).
3. The state validity TTL window ($\tau_{\text{TTL}}$) and innovation anomaly thresholds.
4. Resynchronization protocols for late-arriving or dropped sensor frames.

```yaml
# DOSSIER CHECKPOINT: STATE-01
state_timing_model:
  system_id: "TINYAGENT-SYSTEM-01"
  version: "1.0.0"
  frame_graph:
    root_frame: "world"
    transforms:
      - parent: "world"
        child: "robot_base"
        translation_m: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
        rotation_quat: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]
      - parent: "robot_base"
        child: "camera_optical"
        translation_m: [0.05, 0.12, 0.35]
        rotation_quat: [0.707, 0.0, 0.707, 0.0]
  state_ttl_leases:
    visual_tracking_ttl_ms: 100.0
    proprioceptive_ttl_ms: 10.0
  thermal_limits:
    warning_temperature_c: 85.0
    critical_cutoff_temperature_c: 105.0
    derating_slope_nm_per_c: 0.08
  anomaly_detection:
    innovation_residual_sigma_threshold: 3.5
```
:::

Induce artificial clock drift and measure how timestamp errors generate false velocity estimates. Configure state TTL leases and observe the robot safely freeze when belief uncertainty exceeds safety limits.
